comment: [R89] tests only: the `llm_fast` section the 8 and 16 GB tiers carried until 2026-10-18 (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, the fast-mode add-on). The owner dropped fast mode (docs/FAST-MODELS-2026-10-17.md); the kernel keeps its llm_fast code paths for a manifest that still has one, and the tests inject this section into their own manifests to keep that mechanism covered (llm_model=fast, the add-on fallback, the censored primary of the refusal ladder, the parallel-slot rules).

llm_fast.role: fast mode — the small coder LLM (settings key llm_model = "fast")
llm_fast.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (Q4_K_M, fast mode)
llm_fast.comment: Downloadable add-on [R47]: the 8 GB tier's LLM until 2026-09-28. Selected with vibe.settings.set('llm_model', 'fast') — the kernel restarts llama-server on the selected model; when this add-on is not downloaded the default LLM keeps serving and /api/status reports the fallback. Fast (≈ 40 s per app, 51 tok/s, 5.5 GB VRAM, 4.8 GB RSS) but its generated apps mostly do not work (11/37 functional items in the feature test) — a speed/low-RAM option, not the default. sha256 computed from the local copy 2026-09-28 (the file this OS served since June).
llm_fast.parallel_comment: 2 llama-server slots, each with the full -c above (-c 2*C -np 2 --no-kv-unified) [R72]: two LLM requests at once; CPU-measured 2026-10-06 (docs/PARALLEL-LLM-2026-10-06.md), GPU validation follows the current GPU benchmark
